tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use when a customer reports...'), focuses on symptom/user-facing triggers (ingest failures, egress errors, player 404s, latency, etc.) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly lists trigger contexts including non-obvious ones (401/403/SigV4 errors, CDNAuthorizationStatus Unauthorized, harvest job failures), and explicitly excludes adjacent domains with handoff pointers. It is a longer paragraph but proportionate to the skill's broad scope (v1/v2, many failure modes) and remains clearly organized.
tests.evidence: "Use when a customer reports a MediaPackage problem or when evidence points at the packaging/origin layer: ingest failures or 401/403/SigV4 errors, egress 4xx/5xx, player 404s, origin latency..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific — AWS CLI commands, metric names/dimensions, diagnosis trees specific to MediaPackage v1/v2. It does not explain general concepts like what an API or HTTP status code is.
tests.evidence: v2 uses SigV4 authentication (no per-endpoint credentials). The `IngestEndpoints[].Url` field provides the ingest URLs.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Large lookup tables (metric thresholds, CDN auth detail tables) are moved to references/lookup-tables.md and loaded conditionally; only small tables (e.g. v1/v2 latency dimension tables with 2 rows) remain inline, which is reasonable for core comprehension.
tests.evidence: Table: [Step 2B: v2 ingest health: v2 ingest metrics](references/lookup-tables.md#step-2b-v2-ingest-health-v2-ingest-metrics). Load it when you run this step.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax in the body: lookup-tables.md, secondary-checks.md, access-log-analysis.md, v1-health-checklist.md, v2-health-checklist.md.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific trigger condition (e.g., when customer mentions VOD clips, when content quality is declining, when CloudWatch metrics aren't granular enough), not generic 'see for details' phrasing.
tests.evidence: When the customer mentions VOD clips, Live-to-VOD or harvest job failures, run the harvest jobs section of [references/secondary-checks.md](references/secondary-checks.md).

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use relative 'references/filename.md' format from the skill root with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, destructive-adjacent operations (credential rotation, resets) are called out explicitly as write ops to avoid and escalate with exact warnings, while diagnosis sections use conditional reasoning trees that leave room for interpretation (e.g., 'Question: Is the triggering condition expected').
tests.evidence: These are WRITE operations and are deliberately outside this skill's read-only IAM scope... Recommend it to the customer with the consequence...

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal choices; it prescribes specific AWS CLI commands per version with clear branching logic, not a menu of alternatives.
tests.evidence: Try both v1 and v2 CLI commands in sequence with explicit fallback logic, not an open menu.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable investigation procedure (version detection, ingest/egress diagnosis trees, etc.) applicable to any MediaPackage incident, not a one-off task for a specific channel.
tests.evidence: This skill auto-detects whether the resource is v1 or v2 and branches into the appropriate diagnostic path.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: Gotcha-like facts are embedded throughout (e.g., StatusCode vs StatusCodeRange dimension mismatch, AWS docs typo OuputType, STALE_MANIFEST behavioral nuance), covering non-obvious pitfalls even without a dedicated 'Gotchas' heading.
tests.evidence: **IMPORTANT: AWS docs typo warning.** The v2 dimension for output format is documented as `OuputType` (missing a 't')... CloudWatch dimension keys are case-sensitive.
